The chief places in the Walk were fought out by that redoubtable pair, J. Rathbone and E. Wall, who were receiving the same time allowance from Scratch.

Our pair were still forcing the pace and had gone away a little from the others. Scamell was now 16th, King 23rd and Rathbone, now walking wonderfully well, was our fourth man. Our fate in the team race was now sealed.

…obviously was not fit Green and King were still together and passed in 65 m. 10 secs. Cooper followed, 67.59, then came Rathbone 69 4 and Manning 72 22. At 13 miles King was in trouble and retired shortly after.…

Manning led our men with Green and Rathbone walking very easily in the middle of the field and our 4 others following. A crowd of rain-drenched cyclists waiting at Streatham were surprised to see the leaders so soon, and the hot pace caused our critics to think they could not last.

Rathbone, Reeve and Rickards, all of whom have done some good times in previous championships. Some of our walkers have now transferred their interests to the track, and they will be catered for with a 2-mile club handicap at our Open Meeting on April 28th.

Pollard, Fleming, Macdonald, Rathbone, Briggs, Winner, etc., etc. Several members started javelin throwing towards the end of last season and it is hoped that their interest will revive with the coming of the summer season.
Rathbone completed a promising quartet. At the turn for home (5 miles) the placings were: 1, Surrey W.C., 31pts.; 2, Belgrave H., 62pts.; 3, Sheffield United H., 68pts.
